userStories.title: Add the shared quality checklist and per-function review remit
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give both workflow reviewers the exact shared quality checklist and enumeration instruction, broaden the whole-branch remit, and provide the package-reading note and pure unread-files helper.

**Motivation** — The story review has no checklist for these classes.

**Approach** — One shared checklist (`WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST`). A prompt constant naming eight defect classes, each with the concrete shapes to look for. Both reviewer prompts embed it verbatim, together with an enumeration instruction: walk every function or method the diff adds or changes and judge it against the checklist before giving the `quality` verdict. The story review's existing noise guard stays: a critical or important finding about what the code does carries a verbatim `observed` excerpt.

The checklist text (the constant's content, verbatim):
```
## Code-quality checklist
Judge the changed code against each class. Report only what you can quote from a file.
- Concurrency and atomicity: a check and the write it guards in separate statements or transactions; two writers racing on one row, slot or counter; shared mutable state without synchronisation.
- Data-store semantics: the collation or case-sensitivity of identity and unique columns; uniqueness enforced only in code, not by the store; transaction boundaries; column types and widths against the values written.
- Production wiring: an in-memory, fake or test stand-in on a production path where the project provides a shared implementation (an id or sequence generator, cache, lock, queue, storage).
- Test isolation: a test that depends on state another test created; ordering dependence; shared mutable fixtures; globals, environment or files not restored.
- Input safety: untrusted keys used for object lookup (inherited keys such as __proto__ or constructor); unbounded lengths or sizes reaching storage; unvalidated input reaching a query, path or command.
- Performance: a database or network call per item inside a loop on a batch path; serial awaits that could be one batched call.
- Error handling: a swallowed failure; a result or exit code never checked; a default substituted on error so the caller cannot tell empty from broken.
- Reachability: a list with no way past its first page; a state a user or caller cannot reach or leave.
```

The enumeration instruction (verbatim, in both prompts):
`Before you give the quality verdict, walk every function or method the diff adds or changes and judge it against the checklist.`

Branch prompt remit. The "Do not re-review each story line by line" sentence is removed whole, including its clause after the semicolon ("the story reviews did that, ... is yours to check"). The branch reviewer reviews every required file for the checklist as well as for cross-story contracts. The existing remit bullets (cross-story integration, reachability, consistency, storage against contracts, minor triage) stay, and so do the "What nax already checked" block and `CANNOT_VERIFY_RULE` added by #2535. The prompt's reply shape gains `"inspectedFiles": ["path"]` and the finding field `"observed"`, and the prompt asks for the most severe findings first. The prompt says `List in inspectedFiles every file you read or diffed.` The old package sentence about truncation ("When the diff is truncated, the package ends with \"Files not shown in the diff\" ...") is removed, since the branch package no longer carries a diff.

`BranchReviewPromptInput` gains `readonly range: string`; the prompt names the package as commits, stat and changed files with no diff, gives `git diff <range> -- <path>`, embeds the checklist and the enumeration instruction, drops the do-not-re-review sentence, asks for the most severe findings first, and its reply shape includes `inspectedFiles` and `observed`. `runBranchReview` passes `<seed>..HEAD`.

The "How to read the diff" paragraph is built by `buildBranchPackageReadingNote(range)` in `src/prompts/builders/workflow-branch-builder.ts` (instructional text lives under `src/prompts/builders/`); the writer imports it from `@/prompts`. Its text is:
```
## How to read the diff
No diff is inlined. For each changed file run `git diff <seed>..HEAD -- <path>`, or Read a file the branch added. Start with production source, then migrations and schema, then tests.
```
Substitute the supplied range for `<seed>..HEAD`. US-002 will connect this note to the package writer.

Coverage (`unreadFiles`). A pure helper in `src/operations/workflow-review-coverage.ts` (it lives in `src/operations` because the branch op uses it, and `src/operations` never imports `src/workflow`). An inspected entry covers a required path when, after stripping a leading `./`, it equals the path or ends with `/` followed by the path. `runBranchReview` treats a verdict with no `inspectedFiles` as an empty list. `unreadFiles(required, inspected)` returns the required paths no entry covers, in required order. Entries that match no required path are ignored. US-001 implements and exports the helper; US-002 owns runBranchReview's use of it.

Update existing branch-prompt tests: replace the assertion containing "Do not re-review each story line by line" with one containing WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST, keeping Cross-story integration, Reachability and minorTriage assertions. Replace the "Files not shown in the diff" assertion in the storage-contract test with "git diff seed0..HEAD -- <path>", retaining Storage against contracts, column type and width and migration assertions. Add range: "seed0..HEAD" to the prompt, empty and gateBase input fixtures. Preserve all #2535 verification-fidelity assertions.

**Scope** — In: shared constants, both review-prompt edits, required branch-prompt range and its caller, reading-note builder, pure unreadFiles and their barrel exports/tests. Out: US-002's package writer, required-file classification and unread verdict annotation; US-003's retry policy, feature persistence and readiness consequences. A coverage floor or retry for the story review, the story re-review or the branch re-review — only the whole-branch review gets one. Matching `inspectedFiles` entries in other forms: a package-relative path, a path with a line or range suffix (`src/a.ts:12`), a directory, or a different letter case counts as not covering the required path.

**Interface** —
```typescript
WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST: string
WORKFLOW_ENUMERATION_INSTRUCTION: string
buildBranchPackageReadingNote(range: string): string
unreadFiles(required: readonly string[], inspected: readonly string[]): string[]
```
Create the constants in src/prompts/builders/workflow-quality-checklist.ts and export them and the reading-note builder from @/prompts (src/prompts/index.ts). Export unreadFiles from @/operations (src/operations/index.ts). `buildWorkflowStoryReviewPrompt` keeps the same signature. `BranchReviewPromptInput` adds `readonly range: string`; all its other fields remain unchanged.

routing.reasoning: These are deterministic prompt-string edits, one required range passed by an existing caller, and a pure path-comparison helper; ordinary failing unit tests protect the existing evidence and gate text without introducing a new runtime abstraction.

modifiedFiles.reason: One test asserts the branch prompt contains "Do not re-review each story line by line". US-001 removes that sentence; US-001 owns replacing the assertion with one that the prompt contains `WORKFLOW_QUALITY_CHECKLIST`, keeping the test's other remit assertions ("Cross-story integration", "Reachability", the `minorTriage` shape). The test "checks storage against every declared limit and points at omitted files (nax#2486)" asserts the branch prompt contains "Files not shown in the diff". US-001 removes that truncation sentence because the branch package carries no diff; US-001 owns replacing that one assertion with one that the prompt contains "git diff seed0..HEAD -- <path>", keeping the test's "Storage against contracts", "column type and width" and "migration" assertions. Its prompt-input fixtures `prompt`, `empty` and the spread base `gateBase` build `BranchReviewPromptInput` without `range`, which becomes a required field. US-001 owns adding `range: "seed0..HEAD"` to those three fixtures; no other assertion changes, and the #2535 tests built on `gateBase` keep passing.

userStories.title: Write a complete branch manifest and compute required review files
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace only the whole-branch inline diff package with a status-aware file manifest and calculate the required inspection set used to annotate returned verdicts.

**Motivation** — The cut kept the first 6 of 82 files in diff order, mostly two i18n message files.

**Approach** — Branch review package without a diff body (`writeBranchReviewPackage`). A new writer next to `writeReviewPackage` in `src/workflow/git.ts`. It writes:
```
## Commits (<seed>..HEAD)
<git log --oneline>

## Stat
<git diff --stat>

## Changed files (<count>)
- M packages/nax/src/a.ts
- A packages/nax/src/b.ts
- D packages/nax/src/c.ts
- R packages/nax/src/old.ts -> packages/nax/src/new.ts

## How to read the diff
No diff is inlined. For each changed file run `git diff <seed>..HEAD -- <path>`, or Read a file the branch added. Start with production source, then migrations and schema, then tests.
```

An empty log prints `(none)` and an empty stat prints `(no changes)`, as `writeReviewPackage` does; an empty changed-file list prints `## Changed files (0)` and no lines.

The "How to read the diff" paragraph is built by `buildBranchPackageReadingNote(range)` in `src/prompts/builders/workflow-branch-builder.ts` (instructional text lives under `src/prompts/builders/`); the writer imports it from `@/prompts`.

The changed-file list comes from `git diff --name-status -z <seed>..HEAD -- . <ALWAYS_EXCLUDED>`, one line per record, status letter only (a score is dropped). `R` (rename) and `C` (copy) records carry two paths and print as `<old> -> <new>`; every other status (`M`, `A`, `D`, `T`) carries one. The writer returns the changed paths that still exist at HEAD: deletions are excluded, a rename or copy contributes its new path, a type change (`T`) counts like `M`. The story review, the story re-review and the branch re-review keep `writeReviewPackage` and its inline diff.

The required set (`reviewRequiredFiles`). From the writer's returned paths, nax removes:
- test files, classified per package: the path's owning package is the longest entry of `FeatureContext.packageDirs` that prefixes it, and that package's `resolveTestFilePatterns(...).regex` classifies it; a path under no package dir uses the root patterns (`packageDir` undefined);
- documentation and non-source files, matched on the basename, case-insensitively, at any depth: a basename ending `.md` or `.mdx`; the lockfiles `bun.lock`, `bun.lockb`, `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `Cargo.lock`, `go.sum`, `poetry.lock`, `uv.lock`; image and document files ending `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.svg`, `.ico`, `.webp`, `.pdf`.

`runBranchReview` calls `writeBranchReviewPackage` and then `reviewRequiredFiles` inside the `writePackage` callback it hands `underReviewLimit`, storing the result in a local the op call reads; a throw from either becomes a skipped review (`review package failed: ...`).

What remains is the set the reviewer must inspect. It is deliberately broad: configuration, JSON, YAML, i18n message files and test helpers that do not match the test patterns stay required, since a per-file `git diff` of them is cheap and a wrong value in them is a real defect.

Coverage (`unreadFiles`). A pure helper in `src/operations/workflow-review-coverage.ts` (it lives in `src/operations` because the branch op uses it, and `src/operations` never imports `src/workflow`). An inspected entry covers a required path when, after stripping a leading `./`, it equals the path or ends with `/` followed by the path. `runBranchReview` treats a verdict with no `inspectedFiles` as an empty list. `unreadFiles(required, inspected)` returns the required paths no entry covers, in required order. Entries that match no required path are ignored. Consume the helper exported by US-001 via @/operations.

`runBranchReview(fc, input)` writes it with `writeBranchReviewPackage`, computes `reviewRequiredFiles`, calls the op with `{ prompt, timeoutMs, minorIds, requiredFiles, range }`, and returns the verdict with `unreadFiles` when non-empty. Preserve the verdict's findings. Add readonly requiredFiles and range to WorkflowBranchReviewInput now; the coverage-aware retry policy is US-003's work. Add optional readonly unreadFiles to BranchReviewVerdict; this field is set by runBranchReview, never parsed from the reply. `_workflowDeps` adds `resolveTestPatterns: typeof resolveTestFilePatterns` so tests can inject test-file classification.

Failure behavior: A git call in `writeBranchReviewPackage` exits non-zero: Throws `NaxError` code `WORKFLOW_REVIEW_PACKAGE_FAILED`, as `writeReviewPackage` does; `underReviewLimit` turns it into a skipped review (`review package failed: ...`), and the existing "branch review did not run" reason keeps the PR a draft. `resolveTestFilePatterns` throws for a package: Logged at warn with `storyId: "_run"`; no path in that package is classified as a test file (the required set is larger, never smaller).

Update the shared `input` fixture in test/unit/operations/workflow-branch-review.test.ts by adding requiredFiles: [] and range: "seed0..HEAD", with no assertion changes. Existing runBranchReview tests stub git to return empty stdout: the manifest and required set remain empty, the verdict has no unreadFiles property, and exact { ran: true, verdict } plus seed0..HEAD assertions stay unchanged. Extend existing git and branch-review tests and create review-coverage.test.ts.

**Scope** — In: new whole-branch package writer, per-package required set, resolver dependency injection, branch op input fields, optional unread verdict annotation and production runBranchReview wiring. Out: US-001's checklist, reading-note and pure unreadFiles implementations; US-003's coverage retry, feature record and draft reason. Changing `DIFF_CAP_BYTES`, `writeReviewPackage`, or the packages of the story review, story re-review and branch re-review — they keep the inline diff. Dedicated tests for the empty-log, empty-stat and empty changed-file renderings of the branch package. Per-package overrides of the non-source exclusion list (markdown, lockfiles, images).

**Interface** —
```typescript
writeBranchReviewPackage(projectDir: string, from: string, path: string): Promise<string[]>
reviewRequiredFiles(paths: readonly string[], fc: Pick<FeatureContext, "config" | "projectDir" | "packageDirs">): Promise<string[]>
```
Place reviewRequiredFiles in src/workflow/review-coverage.ts. Extend the existing types with:
```typescript
// WorkflowBranchReviewInput
readonly requiredFiles: readonly string[]
readonly range: string
// BranchReviewVerdict
readonly unreadFiles?: readonly string[]
// _workflowDeps
resolveTestPatterns: typeof resolveTestFilePatterns
```
Read-only integration signatures:
```typescript
resolveTestFilePatterns(config, workdir, packageDir?, options?): Promise<ResolvedTestPatterns>
// ResolvedTestPatterns
readonly regex: readonly RegExp[]
```

[unit] When fc.packageDirs holds both "apps" and "apps/api", reviewRequiredFiles(["apps/api/src/x.spec.ts"], fc) resolves to [] when _workflowDeps.resolveTestPatterns returns regex: [/\.spec\.ts$/] for "apps/api" and regex: [] for other package dirs, classifying the path under apps/api/ with the patterns resolved for "apps/api".
[unit] reviewRequiredFiles(["README.md", "docs/guide.mdx", "bun.lock", "package-lock.json", "go.sum", "img/logo.png", "doc/spec.pdf", "src/a.ts"], fc) with no test patterns resolves to ["src/a.ts"].
[unit] reviewRequiredFiles(["apps/api/bun.lock", "docs/README.MD", "img/Logo.PNG", "src/a.ts"], fc) with no test patterns resolves to ["src/a.ts"] (basename match, case-insensitive, at any depth).
[unit] The file writeBranchReviewPackage(dir, "seed0", path) writes includes buildBranchPackageReadingNote("seed0..HEAD").

[unit] When _workflowDeps.resolveTestPatterns throws for package dir "apps/api", reviewRequiredFiles(["apps/api/src/x.spec.ts"], fc) resolves to ["apps/api/src/x.spec.ts"] and logs one warn entry with storyId: "_run".

[unit] runBranchReview with seed: "seed0", _workflowDeps.git stubbed so diff --name-status -z returns M\0src/a.ts\0M\0src/a.test.ts\0, _workflowDeps.resolveTestPatterns returning regex: [/\.test\.ts$/], and a scripted _workflowDeps.callOp, calls the op with an input whose requiredFiles equals ["src/a.ts"].
[unit] With the same stubs, the op input's range equals "seed0..HEAD".
[unit] With the same stubs and the op returning a verdict whose inspectedFiles is [], runBranchReview resolves to { ran: true, verdict } where verdict.unreadFiles equals ["src/a.ts"].
[unit] With the same stubs and the op returning a verdict whose inspectedFiles is ["src/a.ts"], the resolved verdict has no unreadFiles property.
[unit] With the same stubs and the op returning a verdict object that has no inspectedFiles property, runBranchReview resolves (does not reject) with verdict.unreadFiles equal to ["src/a.ts"].

userStories.title: Retry incomplete branch inspection once and keep unread branches draft
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Use the existing session for one combined parse/coverage retry, preserve the final-turn verdict only when that reply is parseable, and carry unread files into persisted workflow readiness so incomplete review keeps the PR draft.

**Motivation** — Nothing checks how much was read.

**Approach** — Same-session coverage retry. `workflowBranchReviewOp`'s input gains `requiredFiles` and `range`. Its `retry` validates a parsed verdict as complete only when `unreadFiles(requiredFiles, verdict.inspectedFiles)` is empty. On an incomplete verdict the retry prompt is `buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(range, missing)`, which lists each missing path, asks the reviewer to inspect them and re-send the whole JSON object, and says `List in inspectedFiles every file you have read or diffed in this session, not only the new ones.`; on an unparseable reply it stays `buildWorkflowReviewJsonRetry()`. Parse retries run as further turns of the same session (`sendWithParseRetry` re-sends through the session's `send`), so the reviewer keeps what it has read. To build that prompt, `ParseRetryOpts.prompts.invalid` receives the last output: `invalid: (lastOutput: string) => string`. Existing zero-argument prompt functions stay valid. Both `validate` and `op.parse` call the shared shape check `parseBranchReviewReply`; `validate` additionally calls `isCompleteBranchVerdict(verdict, requiredFiles)` (exported next to `unreadFiles`). This is a deliberate, ruled exception (recorded in `.nax/rules/retry-strategy.md`) to the retry-strategy rule that `validate` and `op.parse` share acceptance criteria: coverage decides whether to ask again, never whether the verdict is usable, so `parse` stays lenient and an incomplete verdict is kept rather than discarded. When the one retry is spent, the verdict is kept because `parse` stays lenient: `callOp` takes `op.parse(rawOutput)` of the last reply. `exhaustedFallback` returns `parseBranchReviewReply(lastOutput, minorIds)` as the strategy-level mirror of that, so a parseable but incomplete verdict is kept, findings included. The parse and coverage retries share the one retry turn (`maxAttempts` 2): a reply that is unparseable on the first turn and parseable but incomplete on the second gets no further turn, and that second verdict is kept with `unreadFiles`. The op passes `looksTruncated` so that only an unparseable reply can be treated as truncated: a reply `parseBranchReviewReply` parses always gets the coverage prompt, never `buildWorkflowReviewJsonRetryCondensed()`.

Unread files reach the PR. `runBranchReview` sets `unreadFiles` on the verdict it returns when the list is non-empty. The feature machine's branch-review step stores it as `reviewUnread` on the feature record and writes one ledger note. `publish` passes it to `readinessReasons` as `branchReviewUnread`, which adds a reason, so the PR stays a draft and the advisor's approval is never asked. The verdict's findings go to the branch fix as today. The reason and the ledger note share one formatter, `describeUnread(files)`:
`branch review did not read <N> changed file(s): <a>, <b>, ...` listing at most 5 paths, then `, +<M> more` when there are more.

The new `isCompleteBranchVerdict(verdict, requiredFiles)` returns true when unreadFiles is empty. US-001 creates src/operations/workflow-review-coverage.ts with unreadFiles; US-003 adds isCompleteBranchVerdict to it and exports it through src/operations/index.ts. US-002 adds the requiredFiles/range input and runBranchReview unread annotation; consume those contracts without changing the package writer, classifier, or reply parsers. `ParseRetryOpts.prompts.invalid` is `(lastOutput: string) => string`, called with `ctx.lastOutput`. Existing zero-argument prompt functions stay valid. Build the coverage retry prompt in src/prompts/builders/workflow-branch-builder.ts and export from @/prompts; include `git diff <range> -- <path>` and `Re-send the whole JSON object`. No prompt literal is added outside the prompt builders.

Integration detail: makeParseRetryStrategy invokes its parse callback before validate (src/agents/retry/parse-retry.ts). Use parseBranchReviewReply(output, input.minorIds) for that strategy parse callback and for op.parse; validate receives the parsed verdict and checks coverage with isCompleteBranchVerdict. This is how retry validation shares the string-to-verdict shape check without passing an already-parsed verdict into a string parser. The requiredFiles/range type additions and runBranchReview unread annotation described above belong to US-002; this story consumes them.

Failure handling:
- The reply is unparseable on both attempts: Unchanged: the op returns `null` and the review is skipped as `unparseable reply`.
- The verdict still misses required files after the retry: The verdict is kept with its findings; `unreadFiles` is set; ledger note and readiness reason as in Approach 6.
- The first reply is unparseable and the retry reply is parseable but incomplete: No further turn (the one retry is spent); the retry verdict is kept with `unreadFiles`; ledger note and readiness reason as in Approach 6.
- A parseable but incomplete reply contains text that looks like truncated JSON: It gets the coverage prompt; only an unparseable reply gets the condensed truncation prompt.
- The required set is empty (a branch of only tests and docs): Coverage always passes; no retry for coverage.
- The first verdict is incomplete and the retry reply is unparseable: `exhaustedFallback` sees only the retry reply and returns `null`: the first verdict is not kept, the review is recorded as `unparseable reply`, and "branch review did not run" keeps the PR a draft.
- The coverage retry turn runs past `workflow.timeouts.reviewMs`: Unchanged step-limit behaviour: `underReviewLimit` reports `{ ran: false, why: "timeout" }`, the first-turn verdict is not kept, and the existing "branch review did not run" reason keeps the PR a draft.
For skipped reviews, existing deterministic readiness behavior continues to prevent approval. For a retained incomplete verdict, keep findings flowing to branch-fix even though unread files remain a publish blocker.

Use the existing _workflowDeps, scripted operation and session runtime test seams. Extend test/unit/operations/workflow-branch-review.test.ts for the op retry ACs, including a real callOp two-turn same-session test following test/unit/operations/call-op-retry.test.ts. Extend existing feature-machine, approval and finalize tests for persistence, the shared formatter and the publish seam. The scripted workflowBranchReviewOp verdicts in both `setup` and `scriptB3` in test/integration/workflow/feature-e2e.test.ts carry no inspectedFiles, while their repo changes b.ts after the seed. Add inspectedFiles listing b.ts to each scripted branch verdict so the existing outcome, reasons and call-sequence assertions hold unchanged. The ruled exception is already present in .nax/rules/retry-strategy.md; retain it, with no duplicate rule or hand-edit of generated copies.

**Scope** — In: output-aware invalid-prompt callback, isCompleteBranchVerdict, coverage retry builder and branch op strategy, optional persisted unread state, one shared ledger/readiness formatter and publish propagation. Out: US-001's checklist/remit and unreadFiles implementation; US-002's manifest writer, required-set classifier and runBranchReview annotation. Verifying `inspectedFiles` against the tool audit. The list is self-reported by the reviewer; nax trusts it. A coverage floor or retry for the story review, the story re-review or the branch re-review — only the whole-branch review gets one. Reviewer model selection, pinning or agent fallback. Listing unread files in the PR body beyond the readiness reason. Keeping the first-turn branch verdict when the coverage retry turn hits the review step limit — the review is recorded as not run (timeout), as for any review that times out.

```typescript
buildWorkflowBranchCoverageRetry(range: string, missing: readonly string[]): string
isCompleteBranchVerdict(verdict: BranchReviewVerdict, requiredFiles: readonly string[]): boolean
describeUnread(files: readonly string[]): string

```

routing.reasoning: Cross-module same-session retry semantics and a shared retry API feed persisted readiness decisions; strict TDD isolation follows the session override and protects verdict retention, exhaustion and advisor suppression.

modifiedFiles.reason: the scripted `workflowBranchReviewOp` verdicts (in `setup` and in `scriptB3`) carry no `inspectedFiles`, while the fixture repo changes non-test files after the seed (b.ts, in both `setup` and `scriptB3`, whose repo is built by `setup`). Under US-003 those files are reported unread and the readiness reason turns the expected `outcome: "ready"` into a draft. US-003 owns adding `inspectedFiles` to each scripted branch verdict, listing b.ts (the one file the fixture repo changes after its seed), so the existing outcome, reasons and call-sequence assertions hold unchanged.

analysis:
Goal and completion: close nathapp-io/nax#2532 items A, B and D by deepening workflow story/whole-branch quality review, replacing only the whole-branch inline patch with a complete changed-file manifest, and making incomplete self-reported inspection a deterministic draft reason after one same-session retry. This is an enhancement of packages/nax, not a new subsystem or a change to nax-agent, nax-agent-acp or nax-ai. No implementation files were changed during PRD drafting. Graph-navigation tools were unavailable; findings below were verified with direct reads and text searches.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:17 identifies the shared dependency-injection/error conventions; docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:94 identifies prompt construction as owned by src/prompts. The operations-to-workflow boundary is explicit in packages/nax/src/operations/workflow-types.ts:1: operations owns the reply types because workflow consumes operations, never the reverse. Workflow imports unreadFiles through @/operations; git imports buildBranchPackageReadingNote through @/prompts. Ordering and fidelity: exactly US-001, US-002 and US-003 are retained, each with workdir packages/nax. The binding table states no dependencies for any story, so their dependencies arrays are empty, overriding the narrative dependency notes. The listed implementation order remains the intended handoff: shared prompts/helpers, package/required-set wiring, then retry/readiness. contextFiles reference only files verified on disk, not outputs assumed available through undeclared dependencies. US-003's description identifies the symbols produced earlier so its agent understands those seams. All enumerated ACs are retained in their original story, and failure-table rows not fully exercised by them receive explicit behavioral criteria rather than being silently deferred. This can exceed the narrative maxAcCount split rationale in US-003; the binding three-story structure and required failure behavior are preserved instead of dropping criteria or creating a fourth story. Extra hardening ideas appear only in suggestedCriteria. Refine self-audit: all 23 US-001, 23 US-002 and 23 US-003 explicitly enumerated spec criteria remain in their original story and order, including the observed-rule, still-includes, slash-boundary, case-insensitive-basename, does-not-reject, finding-included and existing-session-pattern regression qualifiers. The four additional US-003 failure-table criteria also remain. All nine failure-table rows map to criteria; all eleven feature exclusions remain verbatim. Each story already has negative paths and backward-compatibility assertions. US-002 root/longest-owner classification criteria now state concrete returned arrays and distinct resolver inputs rather than an underspecified classification claim. US-003's goal now explicitly retains only the final-turn parseable verdict, fixing the draft's misleading last-parseable wording that could have implied caching the first verdict. The shared retry integration is clarified: strategy.parse consumes the raw string, validate consumes that parsed verdict, and op.parse independently uses the same shape parser. Context lists retain the five most critical spec-recommended existing files per story, without adding outputs as inputs; dependencies remain exactly the binding table's empty arrays. Routing is reduced to medium/tdd-simple for US-001's deterministic strings/pure helper and US-002's standard git/resolver integration. US-003 retains complex/three-session-tdd for its cross-module same-session retry/readiness contract and the explicit session strategy override. Main risks are malformed NUL status parsing, score/two-path desynchronization, incorrect package ownership or anchored test regex application, overexcluding real config defects, coverage matches without slash boundaries, null/missing inspectedFiles, treating a valid reply with trailing truncated text as unparseable, retry-budget/session drift, losing findings on an incomplete parseable verdict, and failing to propagate unread state to readiness. Self-reported inspection remains trusted by design; this feature improves review instructions and accountability, not an audit-backed guarantee of review correctness.
